subject: PrivDeploy IaC: flaky CI tests, canary SLOs, and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, security@cedaranalytics.com
Cc: netops@edgevendor.io
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy IaC: flaky CI tests, canary SLOs, and mitigation plan

Team — forwarding Cedar's latest flakiness summary (attached). Cedar is preparing for an on-prem pilot next month and their security lead flagged intermittent terraform/helm failures in our private-stack CI that could mask drift and lead to SLA misses during canary rollouts.

Quick summary:
- CI job ‘priv-iac/e2e’ has ~12% transient failure rate over last 2 weeks, mostly due to helm chart rendering errors and occasional terraform state lock timeouts.
- Failing tests are not consistent — same commit passes/fails across reruns.

Ask: can we propose a short plan to eliminate flakiness, add canary SLO checks, and create a containment strategy so Cedar can still run a limited pilot without risk to production?

Attachments: ci-flakiness-report-20260624.pdf, terraform-plan-privstack.diff, helm-values-proposed.yaml

Suggested quick items to cover in replies:
- Root cause hypotheses for helm & TF flakiness
- CI gating we can add (e.g., stricter linting, deterministic helm rendering, tf plan -out checks)
- Canary SLOs and automatic rollback triggers for private deploys
- Temporary remediation (manual steps or bypass) so Cedar's pilot can proceed while we harden CI

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Cedar Analytics Security <security@cedaranalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: flaky CI tests, canary SLOs, and mitigation plan

Hi Stephanie / Irene — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A couple of clarifications from our side before the pilot: 

1) Risk profile: intermittent CI failures are a problem because they reduce confidence in the canary gate. If a canary passes but the same job flakes on subsequent runs we can't reliably know whether the configuration drifted or if the change itself introduced instability.

2) Required guardrails for pilot:
 - Deterministic plan & apply: we need tf plan outputs checked-in to the pipeline (or at least artifacts) so audit logs show what changed.
 - Chart rendering snapshot: helm templating output must be captured and compared against a golden baseline.
 - Canary SLO: during pilot we expect a 5-min tokenized latency SLO + 99.9% success rate for critical API calls; if canary violates this for 3 consecutive minutes we expect an automated rollback or pause.

We can be flexible on timing if you give us a concrete mitigation plan that includes owners and a rollback/playback approach.

— Cedar Security (M. Ortega)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, security@cedaranalytics.com, netops@edgevendor.io
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: flaky CI tests, canary SLOs, and mitigation plan

Thanks for the callout, Cedar — good, actionable asks. Below is a short, concrete mitigation plan we can implement in the next 10 business days and operate during the pilot. I’ve split into short-term (temporary) and medium-term (hardening).

Short-term (T+1 to T+3 days):
- CI stabilization script: add retry wrappers with exponential backoff around the TF state lock and helm registry pulls. This is only a containment to reduce noise while we root cause. Owner: Mina.
- Artifact capture: store terraform plan -out and helm template output as pipeline artifacts (preserves deterministic render output). Owner: Marcus.
- Canary SLO enforcement: add a lightweight canary monitor that checks the 5-min latency and error budget; on 3 consecutive minute violations we will pause the rollout automatically (platform-level flag). Owner: Stephanie + Platform SRE.

Medium-term (T+4 to T+10 days):
- Deterministic Helm rendering: enforce chart-testing and helm-diff in CI; add a step that performs a deterministic render using pinned chart dependencies and records a SHA of the rendered manifests. Owner: Marcus.
- Terraform plan validation: run tflint + terraform validate + tfsec and require tf plan artifact to be created via terraform plan -out; add a gate that compares plan artifact to the apply artifact in the canary namespace. Owner: Mina.
- Test bisecting & flaky test tracking: instrument the CI to record failing tests and automatically re-run with a bisect script (binary search across commits) to identify the range that introduces flakiness. Create a dashboard for flaky tests to track MTTR. Owner: Irene + CI Eng.
- Conftest/OPA policy checks: add policy-as-code to validate privileged capabilities in helm values (no hostNetwork, restricted hostPath, enforced networkPolicies). Owner: Platform Sec.

Temporary exceptions for Cedar pilot:
- We can allow a manual override to proceed with pilot once the artifact capture and canary SLO enforcement are in place. That means if a CI transient fails but artifacts exist and canary SLOs are satisfied for the first 15 minutes, Cedar may continue. The override will be logged and has to be approved by a designated SRE on-call.

Attachments: I created a proposed pipeline diff (terraform-plan-privstack.diff) and a sample helm-values-proposed.yaml to show policy constraints.

I’ll start the CI jobs today and post logs to the Drive link. If this looks OK to Cedar, we can stand up the canary monitor and permit the pilot to begin with the manual override guardrail.

— Irene Choi
Principal PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, security@cedaranalytics.com, netops@edgevendor.io
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: flaky CI tests, canary SLOs, and mitigation plan

All — quick sync and next steps:

1) I kicked off the CI stabilization branch and uploaded initial artifacts to the Drive link Irene shared (see related_links). Build IDs: priv-ci-3241 (stabilization), priv-ci-3242 (deterministic-render test).

2) Owners & deadlines (compact):
 - Mina: add retry wrappers and terraform plan gate (T+2 days) — deliverable: pipeline patch + test run (attachment: terraform-plan-privstack.diff).
 - Marcus: helm deterministic render + chart-testing (T+4 days) — deliverable: helm-values-proposed.yaml + chart sha verifier.
 - Irene: flaky-test dashboard & bisect script (T+6 days) — deliverable: dashboard link and bisect job.
 - Stephanie: canary SLO monitor + override workflow (T+3 days) — deliverable: runbook & on-call approval flow.

3) Cedar: please confirm the temporary override condition (artifact present + 15min canary ok) is acceptable and whether you want us to run a dry-run pilot next week.

4) I'll schedule a 30-minute handoff on Monday to run through the playbook and show the artifact capture. Proposed time: Mon 2026-06-29 10:00am PDT.

If there are no objections I’ll merge the stabilization branch into a feature branch used by the pilot.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff SRE, Private Deployments
